verdict.rationale: Nix documents per-project environments: `nix-shell` and `nix develop` build or download the declared dependencies and start a shell with all needed environment variables set, and multiple package versions can coexist. These shells must be invoked manually, and nothing in the evidence shows activation triggered automatically on entering a project directory. missing for 10: documented automatic activation on directory entry (cd-hook or direnv-style integration), first-party docs on per-project environment variable configuration, independent corroboration of auto-activation workflows.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the right tool versions and environment variables activate automatically when I enter a project directory

citations.quote: the command `nix-shell` will build or download those dependencies if they’re not already in your Nix store, and then start a Bash shell in which all necessary environment variables (such as compiler search paths) are set.
`nix develop` - run a bash shell that provides the build environment of a derivation
Nix is extremely useful for developers as it makes it easy to automatically set up the build environment for a package.
You can have multiple versions or variants of a package installed at the same time.
